rationale: CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad returned completed/tests_passed with exit 0 and 21 parsed CA_EVENT observations with 0 parsing errors. Indices 17-19 carry the log_types operand for the three rejections and index 20 the summary; together with the Config comment at raft.go:268-271 (the propose-time check may pass while the new configuration is invalid when applied, i.e. it has false negatives by design) they close the question this investigation was opened for. I record an asserted defect claim scoped to availability, promote the log observation as knowledge, and keep the safety half and the documented-acknowledgement counterweight explicit.

knowledge.statement: Observed under isolated execution (CheckRun 880f6a9dbf1e44209e75c837b81e27ad indices 17-19, summary at 20): three nodes consuming their own committed logs in order (applied_before=3 and applying_before=3 for nodes 3 and 1, applied_before=0 for a node rebuilt from persisted state, reapplied_entry=false everywhere) reject a committed entry at index 4, term 2, a single-change joint-entering ConfChangeV2, with the Changer's message 'config is already joint', while their entry sequences are identical: '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2' - normal, ConfChangeV2, normal, ConfChangeV2 - so the log contains a second joint-entering configuration change with no leave-joint entry between the two, and the only intervening entry is a normal one, which is what the target's own propose-time rewrite substitutes for a configuration change it refuses to append. The same run reports violations=0 for at-least-one-leader-per-term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity and applied<=committed, and 245 configuration change proposals produced exactly these three rejections.
knowledge.conditions: Four real raft instances in one process (nodes 1..4, node 4 starting outside the configuration), configuration changes proposed as single-change ConfChangeV2 on the leader with a target drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, half of them with Transition=JointImplicit, application lag that skips one node's apply step about one time in six, node restarts from persisted hard state and applied ConfState, DisableConfChangeValidation left at its default false.

interpretations.rationale: The receipt settles both halves of the question. First, the rejections are not an artifact: each rejecting node consumed its own log in order (indices 17-18 show the batch starting exactly at applied_before+1=4 for nodes 3 and 1; index 19 shows a node rebuilt from persisted state starting at its first entry), reapplied_entry is false in all three, and the nodes were current with their commit index. Second, the log whose entries they consumed is visible and identical in all three cases - '1:t0 2:t2 3:t0 4:t2', i.e. a normal entry, a configuration change, a normal entry, then a second configuration change - so the committed history contains two joint-entering configuration changes with no leave-joint entry between them, and the entry between them is the very shape the propose-time rewrite produces when it refuses to append a change. The consequence chain is then fixed by the target's own code: applying a joint-entering change on a joint configuration is rejected by confchange.EnterJoint, applyConfChange panics on that error ('config is already joint'), and the panic is process-fatal, so a node that is merely applying its committed log in the documented order - the duty doc.go places on the application - cannot make progress past that index. That is an availability defect with a legal trigger (configuration changes proposed through the target's own MsgProp path with DisableConfChangeValidation at its default), an actual producer prefix (leader proposals, replication, commit and in-order application), and no enabled repair: the node cannot skip the entry without violating its duty, and the guard that was supposed to keep the change out consults only the proposing leader's own applied configuration and tracker, which the target's Config comment itself describes as best-effort with false negatives ('the check may pass but the new config may be invalid when it is being applied', raft.go:268-271). Three occurrences in one run at one log position are enough to establish that the shape is reachable; they are not offered as a rate. The safety invariants held throughout (violations=0), so the claim is scoped to availability and to the configuration, ordering and fault assumptions listed: no storage faults, no leader as the rejecting node, and a harness whose application lag is one skipped apply step at a time.
counterevidence: The target documents the mechanism as best-effort with false positives and false negatives, so the proposer-side gap this finding relies on is acknowledged rather than hidden; what the documentation does not provide is a way for the application to keep the node running when the acknowledged gap is hit, and the reaction it documents for an invalid change that reaches apply is a panic.
The rejections come from a single seed and a single log position (seed 35, index 4, term 2); the receipt therefore witnesses reachability, not frequency, and other histories may avoid the shape.

The rejecting nodes are never the leader by harness construction, so this receipt says nothing about a leader meeting the same state, and no node's configuration was observed to change after the rejection because the harness recovers the panic instead of dying.
The safety half is untouched: the same run reports no violation of leadership uniqueness per term, committed (index,term) consistency, committed-index monotonicity or applied<=committed.
limitations: Whether the two configuration entries carry the same or different change sets is not observable from log_types (EntryType only), and the proposer's tracker and applied index at append time were not recorded, so the exact guard evaluation that let the second change through is still unobserved.
The consequence is stated for the panic path in-process: the harness recovers it, so the receipt shows the rejection and the entry sequence, not a node actually ceasing to function.
Storage faults, joint configurations of other sizes, and configurations where the rejecting node is the leader remain outside the event set.

knowledge.assertion: the propose-time guard bounds what the leader appends given its own applied configuration, but a node can still be handed a joint-entering change while its own configuration is joint
